Planxty Davis / Davy - played by Nic Jones on a masterpiece album

Under one of these names, rendered beautifully on guitar by singer - guitarist Nic Jones on his album “Penguin Eggs” - IMHO the best or at any rate equal best (!) to come out of the English trad revival; they didn’t come better, at any rate. Nic’s career was finished by a car crash a long time ago, although he is still alive.
(The penguin eggs feature in a song about whalemen working in the South Atlantic, where these were a treat in their diet.)

Connellan brothers

This is one of the dozen or so surviving tunes composed by Thomas Connellan, an Irish harpist, who spent a lot of time in Scotland around the 1600s and named this tune after the battle of Killiecrankie. Brother of William Connellan - between them they composed over 700 tunes, only a handfull survive

Leonard Barry CD

The latest version I’ve heard of this is by uilleann piper Leonard Barry on his CD “New Road”. His sleeve notes state :
“Planxty Davis was composed by Thomas O’Connellan on the occasion of the Battle of Killiecrankie, fought on July 27th 1689”
He, Leonard Barry, “learned this tune from the great piper Finbar Furey”.

↳ Posted by Kenny on February 16th, 2015.

Re: Planxty Davis

Kimberley Fraser plays this as an air (in A min.) on her ‘Heart Behind the Bow’ cd. Beautifully accompanied by Sheumas MacNeil on piano.
It’s listed as a marching air in Jerry Holland : The Second Collection, edited by Paul Cranford. The accompanying notes tell us that
“The tune first appeared with this title - (Killiecrankie) - in manuscript form in 1694 (Atkinson Ms.). It was later published in Henry Playford’s Collection of Scotch Melodies (London, 1701). Known in most Irish circles as Planxty Davis (O‘Neill, 1903),it appeared in 1742 as The Two William Davises as one of the blind harper O’Carolan ’s compositions.”.
